solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Free to start in 24, it ends in 2015

definitions.note: 20 and 15 across together read DELI VERY, i.e. delivery, the last stage of shipping goods

indicators.note: to free something is to loosen it, so these letters are set loose and rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 24 down, a voting-system clue whose solution is APRON

explanation.surface: A puzzling note about something that begins in one place and finishes in a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' rearranges TO START IN with APRON (24 down). '2015' is not a year: it is 20 across followed by 15 across, DELI + VERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipping goods from place to place finishes when they are handed over, so delivery is where carriage ends.

clue.text: One of The Management has to play a piece of music

parts.note: The Management were the two Rons, a comedy pair played by Hale and Pace, so one of them is Ron
to do a role is to play or perform it

explanation.surface: A member of a company's bosses is obliged to perform a musical number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Management' looks like company bosses, but it is the Hale and Pace sketch duo, two bouncers both called Ron.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form in which a main theme keeps returning between contrasting episodes.

clue.text: When to invade Newcastle area in battle

indicators.note: an invader gets inside, so these letters go into the region named next

parts.note: Newcastle is in the north-east of England, NE
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
by can mean in, as in 'by night'

explanation.surface: A question of timing about an army entering the Tyneside region during a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse gives N(AS)E + BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Naseby, in Northamptonshire, was the decisive 1645 engagement of the English Civil War.

clue.text: Fattest man/woman admits desire to eat, but starter's off

indicators.note: admitting someone lets them in, so the name holds the next part inside it

parts.note: Pat is a name used by both men and women

indicators.note: the starter is the first letter, which is dropped

parts.note: the munchies is a slang term for a craving for food

explanation.surface: Someone owning up to being peckish, but not wanting a first course, ends up the fattest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' pretends to be a first course; it is the first letter of the craving word, which 'but starter's off' removes before 'admits' puts the rest inside the unisex name.
explanation.definitionFit: A paunch is a large belly, so the most paunchy person is the most portly.

clue.text: One of two in a 25's study, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for study is to be heard rather than written

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a piece of research, for instance, by a woodwind player.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is OBOE, which is played through a double reed: two blades of cane bound together.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe's mouthpiece is a pair of cane blades vibrating against each other, so each blade is one of two.

clue.text: A monarch's silk in fancy wardrobe

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rex or regina, king or queen
moiré is a watered silk fabric with a rippled sheen

explanation.surface: A royal's silk garments hanging in an elaborate wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoire is an ornate, often antique, freestanding cupboard for clothes.

clue.text: As one being lit, perhaps?

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A wondering remark about something in the state of catching fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges BEING LIT after I; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something capable of catching fire is exactly what anything being set alight must be.

clue.text: Where there's little this might be unlucky

definitions.text: Where there's little this might be unlucky

parts.words: Where there's little this might be unlucky
parts.note: 13 across holds the word little, and that grid number is traditionally ill-omened

explanation.surface: A superstitious remark that something could be unlucky wherever there is little of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' is the solution to 13 across, so where it sits is that ill-starred number.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirteen is the classic unlucky figure, and LITTLE occupies that slot in this grid.

clue.text: To get better life, move 21 out

indicators.note: out here means in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the solution to 21 down, the word for a child or anyone, is PERSON

explanation.surface: Advice that to improve your life you should move someone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LIFE, MOVE and PERSON (21 down) together.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-improvement is about making yourself a better individual, the same as getting better.

clue.text: 15 13 — stupid clue

parts.note: the dash looks like a minus sign

indicators.note: stupid suggests the word clue is muddled up

explanation.surface: A grumble that a clue is very small and dim.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash is read as a minus sign, MINUS, then 'stupid' rearranges CLUE to CULE. 15 13 is VERY LITTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiny in size is very little; the word also names small lower-case lettering.

clue.text: Note it could be 1 millimetre

definitions.meaning: a half note in music, worth two crotchets
in handwriting a single short downstroke, a tiny mark perhaps a millimetre tall; also any very small amount

explanation.surface: A remark that something may measure one millimetre.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as M IN I M, it also says 'M in 1 M', the milli of a metre.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a half-note musical value and a short pen stroke or tiny quantity.

clue.text: Diamond-shaped crib, broken in short parts

indicators.note: parts here means separates, so the crib letters are split around the inserted piece
broken says the word crib is rearranged
short means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: being in is being at home

explanation.surface: A diamond-shaped cot broken into short pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges CRIB, and 'short' cuts HOME (in) to HOM, which 'parts' the crib letters: R-HOM-BIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is a four-sided figure with equal sides, the shape of a playing-card diamond.

clue.text: Not much is heartfelt till partly rejected

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sincere sentiment kept at the cash desk is not much use, partly turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns back the hidden run ELTTIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A small amount is a direct synonym of not much.

clue.text: Return to normal pad?

parts.note: dap means bounce, and read backwards it gives the word pad

explanation.surface: A question whether a cushion lets you recover your usual form.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: a word for bounce (DAP), taken back, gives the clue's word 'pad'.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover quickly after a setback is to get back to your usual state.

clue.text: Going topless all the same

indicators.note: a word going without its top loses its first letter

parts.note: every means all, as in every one of them

explanation.surface: A shrug that baring one's top is all one to the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an intensifier, as in 'the very same day', it means identical or exactly that.

clue.text: Reason French guards pick up a killer

indicators.note: guarding something means surrounding it, so the French word wraps the next part

parts.note: raison is French for reason

indicators.note: in a down entry, up says the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: to opt is to pick or choose

explanation.surface: A justification for French sentries collecting a murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'up' means the pick word reads upwards; 'guards' then sets it inside the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodent poison is a substance laid down to kill vermin.

clue.text: Rab C's little princess almost helped out

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Rab C Nesbitt is a Glasgow TV comedy character; a daughter of his named after Dido, princess of Tyre, would be Dido Nesbitt

explanation.surface: Rab C Nesbitt's young daughter nearly lent a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Rab C Nesbitt is a scruffy Glaswegian from a BBC Scotland sitcom; his imagined daughter Dido takes his surname, which loses its last T.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing your bit is contributing your share to a joint effort, i.e. pitching in to help.

clue.text: Using best pipe to chase work-shy? Not quite

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the pipe word follows

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter is missing

parts.note: timid means shy
to pipe is to sing in a high voice, like a bird

explanation.surface: Choosing the finest pipe to go after an idle worker, though not entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work-shy' looks like one word but splits into 'work' and 'shy'; 'Not quite' clips the shy word, and 'to chase' puts the pipe word after both.
explanation.definitionFit: Making the most effective use of something is what using it to the best effect means.

clue.text: Right hand that isn't spread across one's diamonds

indicators.note: a meal spread across something lies either side of it, so the next letters go inside

parts.note: a spread is a generous meal
one is I, so one's is I'S
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: At cards, a hand that is not dealt properly spreads across someone's diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like an anagram signal but is a noun, a feast, which 'across' wraps round one's and diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: When cards are dealt incorrectly, the resulting hand is not the right one and must be redealt.

clue.text: In shop, they were all behind me, facing the wrong way

indicators.note: the letters face backwards, so they are reversed

parts.note: if they were all behind me, then I led

explanation.surface: In a shop, a customer boasts of being at the head of the queue, though facing backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a store selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared foods.

clue.text: A child or anyone else

parts.note: per means a, as in fifty pence a kilo
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A list: a young one, or simply somebody else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' looks like an article but means PER, as in 'so much a head'.
explanation.definitionFit: Any individual human, whoever they happen to be, is a human being or individual.

clue.text: Work is accepted by film's number one fan

indicators.note: being accepted by means being taken in, so these letters go inside the film

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's alien film
to go is to work or function

explanation.surface: A movie's biggest admirer is taken on to do a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number one fan' looks like a devotee of a film, but number one is oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone self-centred is devoted to themselves, their own biggest admirer.

clue.text: Fine European soldier will hold on

indicators.note: holding something keeps it inside, so the next piece goes within

parts.note: a soldier ant is a worker caste of ant
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A well-dressed Continental soldier is willing to hang on.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side and the on side are the same half of the field, so on gives LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Graceful and stylish, refined in appearance, so fine in the sense of handsome.

clue.text: A voting system, when standing

definitions.note: noun: a place where aircraft stand

parts.note: PR is proportional representation
on can mean when, as in 'on arrival'

explanation.surface: A question about an electoral method and when it stands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' looks like part of the voting surface but is the definition: the parking area at an airfield.
explanation.definitionFit: At an airport, the hard-surfaced area where planes park and are loaded is called by this name.

clue.text: Order that secures old musical instrument

indicators.note: securing something holds it in place, so the honour wraps the next letter

parts.note: OBE is the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: An instruction that locks up an antique musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-reed woodwind instrument with a penetrating tone.

clue.text: No right to make certain of result

indicators.note: no right means the letter for right is taken away

parts.note: to ensure something is to make certain of it

explanation.surface: Having no entitlement to guarantee an outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to follow on as a consequence is to result.

clue.text: Where to eat cheese, keeping protest short

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it, so the cheese goes round the next piece

parts.note: brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: short means the last letter is lost

parts.note: to protest innocence is to assert it

explanation.surface: A restaurant tip involving cheese and a cut-short protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protest' suggests complaint, but here it means declare, as in protesting innocence; 'short' clips it and 'keeping' sets it in the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal French-style restaurant serving simple meals.

clue.text: In clink, anger of criminal being held to account

definitions.note: a noun phrase naming the event of being called to answer

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are crooked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A prisoner's fury in jail as he is made to answer for his crimes.
explanation.definitionFit: Judgement Day, when all must answer for their deeds, is the ultimate calling to account.
